candidate.sense: An edible starchy root with sweet flesh.

claims.proposition: In Indonesian, “ubi jalar” denotes sweet potato, also known as ketela rambat.
“Ubi jalar” is commonly understood in Indonesia for sweet potato.
“Ubi jalar” is a clear standard everyday Indonesian term for the specific sweet potato, while “ubi” alone can be broader.
Keledek or ubi keledek refers to sweet potato.
Keledek is commonly used and understood in Malaysia for sweet potato, particularly in food contexts.
Ubi keledek is an explicit normal Malaysian Malay term, with keledek also common as a shortened everyday form.
For sweet potato, Indonesian commonly uses “ubi jalar” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “keledek” or “ubi keledek”; these are different everyday terms for the same root.

context.scope: Common concrete household and food objects with clear single-sense English cues; prioritize recognizably different Indonesian and Malaysian spellings or clearly preferred everyday terms; avoid concepts in existing batches
